sentenceSets.sentence: A cohesive team needs not just shared goals but shared trust, which takes time to develop.

answerChoices.reasoning: Unity can be imposed from above by a common command, but the sentence says what holds this team together must be built between its members over time.
Harmony describes an absence of friction, while the sentence points to the bonds of trust that keep members working as one.
Effectiveness is measured by results, whereas the sentence is describing what makes the group hold together in the first place.
Loyalty runs from each member toward the team, but the sentence describes trust flowing among them and binding the group internally.
Diversity concerns the range of people involved, not the bonds between them that the sentence says take time.
Ambition is already covered by the shared goals the sentence says are not sufficient.
Experience accumulates individually, while the trust described is something built between people.
Discipline comes from rules and habit, but the sentence attributes the quality in question to mutual trust.
A team pulling apart is the opposite of one held together by trust.
The sentence says the necessary trust takes time to develop, which a short-lived group would never gain.
People who do not know one another cannot build the trust the sentence requires.

sentenceSets.sentence: The exhibition felt less like a survey than a cohesive argument, each room extending the claim made by the one before.

answerChoices.reasoning: Coherence means the argument can be followed without contradiction, but the sentence describes rooms that actively build on one another into a single connected whole.
Sustaining an argument is a matter of keeping it going, while the sentence emphasizes how the parts lock together as each room extends the last.
Persuasiveness concerns whether the visitor is convinced, whereas the sentence describes how tightly the sections are joined.
Linearity means merely proceeding in order, but the rooms here are said to develop one another rather than simply follow in sequence.
Exhaustiveness is exactly what a survey offers, and the sentence sets the exhibition against a survey.
Ordering by date would organize a survey, while the connection described is one of claim and extension.
Elegance describes style, whereas the sentence explains how each room relates to its neighbor.
Polemic implies attacking an opposing view, but nothing in the sentence sets up an opponent.
Rooms that each extend the previous claim are the opposite of scattered.
The sentence describes an argument being made, not the absence of one.
An argument developed room by room to its conclusion is not incomplete.

sentenceSets.sentence: Without a binder the powder never becomes cohesive, and the tablets crumble in the bottle before they reach a pharmacy.

answerChoices.reasoning: Solidity describes the state of matter, but the missing binder is what would make the particles cling to one another instead of falling apart.
Compactness is achieved by pressing material together, whereas the sentence says the failure is the absence of something to hold the grains to each other.
Durability is resistance to wear over time, while these tablets fall apart because nothing joins their particles at all.
Uniformity concerns even distribution through the mixture, but the tablets crumble for want of anything binding the grains together.
Dissolving is what a tablet should do once swallowed, not what keeps it intact in the bottle.
Freedom from contamination has nothing to do with tablets breaking apart in transit.
Strength of dose is unaffected by whether the powder holds its shape.
Remaining granular is the problem the binder is meant to solve, not the goal.
Nothing in the sentence concerns harm to the patient, only the tablets falling apart.
Smell has no bearing on whether the powder holds together.
A liquid could not be pressed into tablets at all.
